activity.notes: Kuikuro oral history and linguistic documentation identify Ihikutaha, together with Mütsümü/Mâcâmâ, as a chief involved in the fission from Oti and the formation of the Kuikuro local group and village. The Kuikuro lexicon places Oti's joint Kuikuro-Matipu occupation probably until the middle of the nineteenth century. ATLAS therefore uses c.1850 as a narrow representative point for Ihikutaha's documented founding activity, not as a fabricated lifelong chiefship or a claim that all Kuikuro history began in one exact year.

sources.title: Kuikuro Lexicon — DOBES / Max Planck documentation
sources.citation_text: The Kuikuro lexicon states that founder chiefs Mütsümü and Ihikutaha left Oti to seek another place and that Oti was occupied by shared Kuikuro/Matipu ancestors probably until the middle of the nineteenth century.

sources.title: Mutua Mehinaku, Tetsualü: pluralismo de línguas e pessoas no Alto Xingu — UFRJ/FUNAI
sources.citation_text: The thesis preserves Kuikuro oral-history passages naming Ihikutaha as a young chief who joined the founding group at Kuhikugu and describes the village-formation process.

review_context.correction_note: Register the documented Kuikuro founder chief with a c.1850 representative point; do not treat 'Kuikuro Civilization' as a centralized state with a continuous sovereign reign.
